Budget colours: green through 9 min · yellow 10–13 min · red >13 min.

Planning scenario: 16 minutes of water supply. An 8-minute one-way drive uses the full 16 minutes for a return trip before filling, unloading, setup or other delays. Colours follow the selected time budget from the chosen origin; they do not predict water remaining or mutual-aid arrival.

Green road sections fit the time budget using distance ÷ assumed speed. This is not validated emergency response coverage. It excludes traffic, grades, vehicle constraints and water setup time. Closed / unknown-speed roads are excluded.

Cluster screening assumptions

5 homes / 5 km are editable example thresholds, not fire-service standards. Distances are straight-line screening estimates. The Buildings KML supplied the study outline. Microsoft footprints now provide structure geometry; residential use, occupancy and township assignments remain unverified.

Home clusters

Candidate areas

Candidate points identify areas to investigate, not surveyed installation locations. Check all-season tanker access, turning and staging, drafting connection, refill source, land access, ground conditions and maintenance. Capacity and installation need a separate technical assessment.

Hydrant & cluster evaluation

ALL BUILDINGS

Analyse detected structures against the Searchmont Resort hydrant. Distances follow imported roads; building use and tanker access remain unverified.

Route assumptions

Buildings and the hydrant are projected onto their nearest included road segment within this limit. The connecting gaps are straight-line approximations; their distance and time are excluded from the road leg. This run uses ORN roads regardless of the Coverage toggle, plus non-demo manual routes. Local exclusions and speed overrides apply. Unreviewed roads are assumed passable; source speed limits cap the assumptions.

Waiting for source data…

Cluster settings

Fixed-radius groups: choose the densest remaining building-centred circle, assign each building once, then repeat. Every member is within the chosen radius of its centre. Circles can overlap; membership does not. Groups use straight-line proximity and may span roads, rivers or other barriers. This is structure clustering, not household counting.

● ≤5 min ● 5–10 ● 10–20 ● >20 ● unresolved

Building results

Distances and times are for the selected route to the road projection of the hydrant. Access gaps, fill time and turnaround are excluded.

Each detected structure has a stable footprint ID and a short B-number for this extract. Road connections, turn restrictions, current passability and access paths need validation before operational use.

ABOUT THIS WORKSPACE

Local knowledge, made visible.

This prototype contains a real Esri topographic background and 21 locations imported from Searchmont FD - Water Sources.kmz: 20 water locations and the fire hall. The resort hydrant is the one existing source identified by the user. Other water locations are recorded as drafting locations; their notes and verification needs are preserved. Fictional sample roads can be shown separately.

Drafting can tie up people and equipment. Each water record therefore keeps people, equipment, setup time, preference and access notes separate. Unknown values stay unknown.

Coverage uses manual road records and, when enabled, imported ORN segments. Imported roads join only at matching original vertices (coordinates rounded to six decimal places); geometric crossings alone are not connected. Source direction fields are respected where recognised. Manual drawing can snap nearby endpoints. It does not route over background map roads. When enabled, the ORN scenario uses imported line geometry with explicit user assumptions. It is not a certified routing network: connectivity, turn restrictions, grade separation, blocked passages, structures, load limits and real-time access have not been validated. Water setup time is stored separately and is not included in the road coverage calculation.

The uploads Buildings in Searchmont.kml and Roads in Searchmont.kml each contain one polygon: Response Area and Searchmont and Area respectively. They are displayed as user-supplied study outlines, not verified response jurisdictions or township boundaries. Neither upload contains individual buildings or road centre lines; building geometry has since been added separately from Microsoft Canadian Building Footprints. The road summary is retained as unverified reference information and is excluded from travel calculations. Separate ORN Composite segment geometry has now been imported from the linked service for a buffered rectangular window around the Response Area. Full intersecting segments are retained. ORN source attributes are kept separate from local planning overrides. The imported snapshot is not a live road-condition service. Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Ontario. No terrain raster has been imported, so road gradients have not been calculated.

The Evaluate tab computes routes from every building centre toward the resort hydrant using projected points on the nearest included road segment. Point-to-road gaps are reported separately and excluded from road distance and time. Results therefore describe road legs rather than complete driveway-to-hydrant journeys. Cluster radius is straight-line distance around a building-centred circle. The evaluator greedily selects the densest remaining circle and assigns each building at most once; it is not a globally optimal grouping. All structures are considered, regardless of verified residential use. The evaluator uses its own visible speed assumptions and the local road exclusions, independently of the Coverage toggle.

Edits remain in this browser, not a shared database. Export GeoJSON to keep a portable copy. Water, facility, home-cluster and proposed-storage records are exported separately. Proposed storage is never counted as available water. Cluster screening compares user-entered home counts and straight-line distance to the existing hydrant. It does not infer homes from imagery or identify engineering-ready sites. Microsoft building footprints are displayed separately as unclassified structures. The extracted subset retains complete footprints whose centres fall inside the Response Area outline. Nearby structure counts use footprint centres and an explicit circular radius, not road distances or household counts. Microsoft reports varying imagery dates and imperfect detection; local completeness has not been validated. The original repository is archived. Building data is available as a separate GeoJSON download with Microsoft attribution and an ODbL notice. Township names are user-assigned; township boundaries have not been imported.
